key_insight: CalTwin combines a Fisher-information shift penalty with a confidence-misalignment penalty to make medical world models both more robust to hospital-to-hospital distribution shifts and better calibrated.
clinical_relevance: This could improve the reliability of latent-patient forecasting used in digital-twin planning and imaging-based decision support, especially when models are deployed at unseen hospitals.
method: GRU-based medical world model with a latent transition predictor.
Adds Fisher-Information-based regularisation to reduce covariate-shift sensitivity across fragmented training data.
Adds a Confidence Misalignment Penalty to reduce overconfident multi-step forecasts.
evidence_signal: On PhysioNet 2019 Sepsis Challenge data, using two hospital systems for training and a third unseen system for OOD testing, CalTwin reduced OOD next-step latent-state MSE by 9.1% versus the baseline and slightly improved calibration (ECE down 0.7%).
watch_item: The calibration gain was small, so the approach may need further validation across more sites, tasks, and deployment settings before clinical use.
paper_title: CalTwin: Towards Calibrated, Shift-Robust Medical World Models via Fisher-Information Regularisation
